utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You wish to raise something, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour. It's in connection with a document that was listed as a potential Defence exhibit to be used with this witness during his direct testimony; it was not. I wanted to do -- ask some questions about it in cross-examination, also because there was some confusion for me about whether or not this exhibit which is 3D695, whether it is something that was going to be part of the Defence request for documents to be admitted from the bar table. And I have some foundational questions about the document. It's not been translated into English, and actually I will request to go into private session because I understand from Mr. Visnjic he got it from the government under certain restrictions and I think one of those includes not discussing some matters about it in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I don't know if you've been misinterpreted here, Mr. Hannis, you say that this document was listed as a potential Defence exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: To be used with the witness during his direct testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And it wasn't used in --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It was not used.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay. There's nothing to stop you cross-examining on it, is there?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But Mr. Visnjic advised me that he received this document from the government with certain restrictions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So the only issue is private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. I thought it was sounding more complex than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, I think that's -- I think that's all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Visnjic, is this a document that has to be dealt with only in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, for the time being, yes. I will explain what the restrictions are and then you can make your decision on the basis of this explanation. But we must do that in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. Are you about to deal with the document at this stage, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: It was one of the first things I was going to ask the witness about. There's some foundational matters I wanted to do with him in the event that upon reading the English translation I find that something that would want the Court to consider.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, before we go into private session for that purpose, I just want to acknowledge the presence of Mr. Ackerman. I know there were some difficulties facing you this morning and we're extremely grateful to you for the effort that's been made to facilitate the court sitting this afternoon. So we'll now go into private session and hear what Mr. Visnjic has to say.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, this is a document, it is the war diary of the Supreme Command Staff that we received from the National Council, or rather, the Government of Serbia subject to certain restrictions, that would be the ban on the use of the document in its entirety. There's also the ban and prior notice to them that the document would be used. Unfortunately, I don't have this document with me, the official document, so I'm quoting from memory now. But this is the first thing that came to my mind when Mr. Hannis asked me that. They allowed us to use the document but only in part, not in its entirety. To my mind this restriction is as it is on face, we have to take it at its face value, I can't tell you anything less or more than that. We listed this document for use with some of the witnesses, but when we translated it we decided not to do that. The first reason is that it is a handwritten document, it has not been translated in its entirety, and the witnesses already indicated that this is a document that is much narrower in its scope than the combat operation -- combat reports that we intend to submit to the Court. So to avoid duplicating the documents, we withdrew this document from our list that we -- of the documents that we wanted to use, and this was not in the title. This document was left in the request for the documents that we intended to file from the bar table -- to tender from the bar table, but that was a mistake, this was done by mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, nothing that you've said so far needed to be said in private session. Are you actually unaware of the detail at the moment of the restriction on the use of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, if you give me ten minutes I can find it somewhere in my files, but the only problem is that Mr. Hannis brought this up a minute ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Hannis, can we side-step it until Mr. Visnjic gets ahold of what he has? It may be that it doesn't matter because you happen to be aware of it and have it, and that may be the complete answer. But I suspect you would rather try to use it within the confines of the restriction that's been imposed in its handing over.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I would rather use it without any restrictions at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, yeah, it may come to that, but let's find out what the restriction is first of all. If you can live with the restriction, then there's no point in going beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I agree. I'll set it aside until I finish everything else and ask do come back to it at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well. Please deal with that as a matter of urgency, Mr. Visnjic, and we'll meanwhile continue with cross-examination of the witness on other matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. [Open session].

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Pending resolution of an issue outstanding following that discussion we shall continue in open session with the cross-examination of Mr. Curcin.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Curcin.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Mr. Bonomy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your cross-examination by Mr. Hannis will now continue. Please bear in mind that the solemn declaration to speak the truth which you made at the beginning of your evidence continues to apply to the evidence today until it finishes. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Welcome back, General. The first document I wanted to ask you about is Exhibit P1483, and I've got a hard copy I can hand to you. It is dated the 12th of April, 1999, and it's entitled: "A supplement to directive DT number 22-1 of 9 April 1999." Do you recall, sir, that document that this is a supplement to, the directive of the 9th of April?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the question I have for you on this one is in the next-to-last paragraph it talks about some changes to be made, and one of them -- the first one says: "Paragraph 5 shall be added behind paragraph 4 to read: 'To break and finally expel the aggressor from the Z/O,'" is that the zone of operations? Can you tell me what that abbreviation stands for?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there's no abbreviation in my version. "In order to expel the aggressor from the zone of responsibility."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. We have an abbreviation in English. "Subsequent to the development of the situation on the war front, you shall be strengthened by the," and then I have an acronym, "KK, plan its use on time." Can you tell me what KK stands for there?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Kragujevac Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Then it goes on: "And paragraph 6 to read: 'Forces of the MUP and civilian defence shall be placed under the command of the 3rd Army during the operation and they shall be used exclusively by your decision.'" So on the 12th of April it was contemplated that the MUP and civilian defences would be under the command of the 3rd Army, correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And this is even -- this is about six days before that order we saw from supreme commander calling for the subordination of the MUP for combat activities, correct? Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And if you allow me, one of the tasks of the chief of the Supreme Command Staff, a few days before the 12th of April at the evening collegium meeting when the situation at front was analysed, was to examine the possibility of the resubordination of MUP to the army. So this is something that had been contemplated earlier. This was not something that came to it maturity on the 12th.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I recall you told us and I think we saw in some of the evening briefing notes that there were discussions about that with I think the Ministry of Justice and I think the MUP as well. Can you tell us who else was involved in those discussions? The minister of defence?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Not the Ministry of the Interior. A memo was sent from the legal administration in the General Staff to the Ministry of Justice to provide a legal interpretation for the possibility of such a resubordination, but they then returned it to the federal defence ministry because they believed that they were the tactical mainstay and that the justice ministry has no jurisdiction over this issue. The MUP was not consulted about this idea at all as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I accept that. As far as you know, the MUP was not consulted. Next I want to ask you some questions regarding your statement, General. This is Exhibit 3D1121, and I have a hard copy I'll ask the usher to hand you. And the first paragraph I want to ask you about is paragraph 9, and in that paragraph you tell us that in your job you studied the combat reports and you paid special attention to the combat reports of the 3rd Army. And you told us that none of those combat reports talked about anyone taking away identity documents or personal documents from the Kosovo Albanians, correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you also said there were no reports on attacks on the civilian population, and does that include no reports of attacks on the civilian population by MUP personnel or are you referring only to attacks by VJ personnel?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The combat reports of the 3rd Army command contained information relating to the 3rd Army. So on the part of the 3rd Army personnel, there were no such things. The reports did not go on to describe the MUP actions.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Further on in your statement in paragraph 22 you talk about some other kinds of reports. There's a mention, the English translation mentions a BI report. Can you tell me what the -- those initials BI stand for. Is that a security report?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there's no abbreviation in my text. I assume that this would be combat report, "borbeni izvestaj" that could be the abbreviation BI, yes, it is true. It says here: "There were no reports about any incidents involving those problems in any combat reports." So that would be the abbreviation for combat report.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And likewise it says there were no reports. I want to ask you now if you could take a look at Exhibit P1459. I don't think this is entitled: "Combat report," but it appears to be a report from the 3rd Army command. It's dated the 25th of May, 1999, and this is a report from General Pavkovic in essence complaining about the non-subordination of MUP to the VJ. Have you seen that document before today?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman showed it to me I believe last time that I testified, and I saw it during the proofing for my evidence here now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And am I correct that your evidence is that during the time during the war when you were working you never saw this report come into the Supreme Command Staff?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This report that I see in front of me I did not see during war.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, is that the kind of report that you would have seen, given your job and the nature of this report?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have seen it and it would have been discussed at the evening briefing so that I really can't understand why, for one, I never saw it and why this was not discussed at any of the evening briefings.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could go to page 2 of the English. And I don't know if paragraph 4 is on the bottom of that B/C/S page or if we have to go to the second page of the B/C/S, yes. Yes, could we go to page 2 of the B/C/S as well?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I want you to look at paragraph 4 and let me read that to you and ask you a question. It says: "It has been established beyond doubt and we have already reported on it in regular combat and other reports, that due to the non-compliance with the resubordination orders some MUP members and to a considerable extent entire smaller units, which 'operate' independently on the ground are committing more serious crimes against the Siptar civilian population in settlements or refugee shelters - murder, rape" et cetera. So here he seems to be saying that the 3rd Army has already reported about this in regular combat and other reports. Now, that's not consistent with what you told us before, that you never saw any combat reports mentioning those kind of crimes being committed against the civilian population. So can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, of course. If you are referring to this report, I did not see it. If you mean to say that this claim is correct, could you please verify that because I state with full responsibility that no report, no combat report from the 3rd Army from the time-period of the war contained such information. There was only one case in Kosovo Polje, three soldiers, conscripts, who were drunk left their unit with their weapons and they killed two Albanians, civilians. They were arrested, they were tried, and convicted. There is a report on that, it is contained in a regular combat report, but apart from that there are no reports about the incidents that are mentioned here in paragraph 4, and it is easy to check that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you saw those reports on a daily basis, correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me take you to paragraph 25 through 27 of your statement, and you mention daily operation reports and combat reports were studied. You explained how the operation -- or the duty operations team drew up combat reports every night and by 0600 forward them to General Ojdanic and his deputies and others. You mentioned that those reports were then forwarded by the office of the Chief of Staff of the Supreme Command to the military office for President Milosevic. Do you know to whom in the military office those reports went?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: The president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, not President Milosevic. It says in my text president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, that's number one.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But that was President Milosevic, correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't say that here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But he was?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: We're talking about the function, we're not talking about a person, but he was, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And --

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the chef de cabinet of the chief of the Supreme Command Staff sent this to the chef de cabinet of the president of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, General Susic, so he received a certain number of combat reports.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Do you recall when Susic became a general? I had seen some documents referring to him as a colonel. Do you know when he got promoted from colonel to general?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was a colonel-general at the time, so perhaps there may have been an error there at one point, but he became a general a long time before I did, in fact.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: That may have been my mistake or a mistake on the document I was looking at. Thank you. All right. Let me ask you next about other than the office of the FRY president, did those reports go to anyone outside the VJ?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. They went to the defence minister, Mr. Bulatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And no one else as far as you know?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the initial question because I'm no longer sure whether I understood you right. Who received -- well, every combat report, the original, stated on the last page which copy of the combat report went to whom, the first one went to the archive, the second to the Chief of Staff, and so on and so forth. So it may have changed, but whoever a copy was addressed to received that particular copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. Thank you. All right. Now, let me go to some of your testimony when you were here on the 5th of October, and you recall you told us about meeting with General Ojdanic in connection with this -- this Joint Command order that we were talking about. And this is Exhibit P1487.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: If we could have that up for a moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And correct me if I'm wrong, General, but I think you told us that you first became aware of this on the 17th of April, when you were called in by General Ojdanic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned what, I became aware of the existence of the Joint Command or something else? I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You became aware of the existence of this map with a reference to a Joint Command order for operations in the area of Rugovo.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, now I understand you. Yes, that is correct. That night, on the 17th of April, that was the first time that I saw an excerpt of this map at General Ojdanic's.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. I want to go through that with you in a little bit of detail because it's -- this document has been a bit of a mystery for me, and you're the first one who's been able to tell us such specifics about it. You referred just now and I think last time you were here to an excerpt of a map. Can you tell us how big of a map are we talking about? Are we talking about something the size of this paper I have in my hand, A4-sized paper? Are you talking a full 1 metre by 1 metre map that goes on the wall? What kind of size of a map are we talking?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: A3, that would be the size of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And you mention it had some writing on it, including a reference to Joint Command order number such and such, correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I can recall, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But there was nothing else other than the map, there wasn't a separate order attached to it or any text document. Is that what -- is that how you recall it?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, precisely. I never saw any orders, commands, or any attachments to that map.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And was it only the two of you? Was it just you and General Ojdanic in his office looking at this map and talking about it? Nobody else present?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just the two of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you told us that General Ojdanic told you that this is something that he had received or gotten from General Pavkovic, right?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Did -- this seems a little strange to me. You said that Ojdanic told you Pavkovic came in with this map and Pavkovic had sometime shortly before that been to see President Milosevic, correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Didn't that strike you as rather odd, that General Pavkovic, who was a subordinate to General Ojdanic, has gone to see the supreme commander first and then brings this map in to General Ojdanic?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes and no. You know --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: President Milosevic was able to invite directly any one of the commanders and talk to them and issue them with assignments, even bypassing the chief of the Supreme Command Staff. However, it was the practice and the rule that after that the person who had been invited to see the superior goes to the Chief of Staff and report. That was my understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. And in paragraph 17 of your statement you talk about that, that you describe General Ojdanic as a principled man who did not breach subordination. He requested the same of his subordinates and you mentioned in such cases you would inform your superior about the assignment or order received or if your immediate superior wasn't available you would tell him when he came back. So this is sort of out of the ordinary chain of command, this kind of event, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can't put it that way, but I have already tried to explain that it was customary way if one was invited by the superior and the immediate superior is informed of it -- for instance, that evening when this suggestion was written, my superior was not on the command post, he was not easily reachable, so General Ojdanic called me directly. And I later informed him that I had been there, that I had done that, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in those circumstances, would General Ojdanic tell your immediate superior that he, Ojdanic, had called you in to assign some task to you, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The first opportunity he had by telephone or in person, why not.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, you told us that in connection with this map that General Ojdanic wrote up the suggestions that are in Exhibit P1487, and you explained to us that you were able -- that he was able to do that or the two of you were able to do that without any reference to a written order, correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And you told us that you had it -- you had the telegram prepared, you brought it back to General Ojdanic, who noticed a mistake, and he inserted the missing word in handwritten black ink, correct? You wanted to go back and have it typed up, but --

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in black pen. You see it right there. This is a signed -- this is a photocopy of the original which I had taken to be signed. You see the last line.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And you said that the reason for that was because I guess -- was it General Ojdanic who thought it was too urgent, that this had to be done right away and there wasn't time to go have it typed up again; is that fair?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, especially because this telegram was going to be encrypted and the encryption would involve that word too as an integral part of the text, so that the recipient, the command of the 3rd Army, would receive the text, including this word, and we were aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And what was the word that was inserted?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Implement. If you want me to read the whole sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I deem it useful to have our suggestions reviewed comprehensively and that you adjust your position and the disposition of forces in order to prevent a new spill-out and thus implement or achieve your fundamental objective: Destruction."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, before today have you ever seen the Joint Command order number 455-148 that is referred to in these suggestions? Did anybody show it to you when you prepared for your testimony or did you see it or hear about it when other witnesses testified here?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we have the usher assist me, and I'll hand the witness a hard copy of Exhibit P1878.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, this is the document the Joint Command order 455-148 of 15 April 1999. Now, I think Judge Bonomy asked you a question about this, too, regarding your ability to or General Ojdanic's ability to draw up suggestions without seeing anything other than the map and what limited writing was on it. In particular he did ask you about the item number 3 in the suggestions which is to delay stand-by for action. Could you look at paragraph number 5 which is: "Task of the units." Do you find that? That's page 3 of the English. I'm not sure what page it is for you. Do you find that? And immediately above that there's a heading called: "Readiness," and --

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Above?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And the -- and the second one says: "For breaking up and destroying of the Siptar terrorist forces in the Rugovo sector at 0600 hours on 18 April 1999." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: There wasn't any information written on the map about what time that operation was scheduled to begin, was there?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember this, and I believe I said that last time. In response to somebody's question here I said it's possible that below the heading "readiness" might be indicated as well. The practice went that on the map under the text there would be a heading "readiness," such and such a day, such and such an hour. So I thought that perhaps it was written on the map, readiness at 0600 hours on 18th April 1999. You find it on maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. So are you telling us now you remember that that time of 0600 on the 18th of April was written on the map?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't say that the last time either, and I'm not saying it now. I'm just reading what is written in this paragraph, and I believe it's possible, even likely, that it was written on the map then. But I'm not claiming it was because I really don't recall.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: In answer to some of the questions from Mr. Fila about the map, you indicated that this was strictly a military operation and that there wasn't any involvement of MUP or civilians, correct? Do you recall being asked a question about that and giving that answer?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I remember I was examined, but I don't remember the exact questions or answers. And in particular I don't think I mentioned civilians nor were they mentioned in the text, in the order, in that context. Maybe you mean something different.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Let me take you directly then to the question and your answer. At page 16980, line 9, Mr. Fila said: "To conclude with this document before you, both the map and this document and what General Ojdanic dictated into it," and that's referring to 1487, the suggestions that General Ojdanic wrote up, "to conclude with is it a military operation or some sort of mixed operation? Is there a mention of any civilians or the MUP?" And your answer was: "This was a purely military operation." Do you recall now being asked that question and giving that answer?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Could you look at paragraph 4 -- no, I'm sorry, first let's go to paragraph 2. Could you look at paragraph 2 of Exhibit 1878, task of the Pristina Corps. Do you find that, General?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Point 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes. It says: "The Pristina Corps with the reinforced" --

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: "With the reinforced and armed non-Siptar population of Kosovo and Metohija is to support MUP forces in breaking up and destroying the Siptar terrorist forces in the zone of responsibility." So this is a joint operation, isn't it, with both the MUP and the armed non-Siptar population, the civilians, correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. This refers to the entire of the Pristina Corps, the area of responsibility of the whole Pristina Corps, not this operation in Rugovo. If you allow me, in point 2 we see the assignment, the task, of the Pristina Corps; and later on assignments to units are listed, paragraph 5 and further on. So this task was received from the superior command, the command of the 3rd Army, or they formulated it itself. In some places perhaps there were indeed those joint actions involving armed population and unarmed Albanian population, but I haven't yet reached para 6. If you want me to read on, I will.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, if you could go down two --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I see Mr. Fila on his feet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just to clarify, Your Honour, I neither showed this document nor did I examine the witness on it. So this is leading the witness. I examined the witness on a document entitled "suggestion," something drafted by General Ojdanic. This was not drafted by General Ojdanic. I do not understand this line of questioning. I don't mind the question, but not in my context because I have not even seen it let alone examined on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the question related to what the operation was, whether it was a joint operation or not. The witness has said it was a purely military operation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Fila's objection is to your attributing to him the raising of this issue, and he maintains he didn't raise it. He's not objecting to your question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I think the question was raised by the witness's answer, not necessarily Mr. Fila's question, but I pointed to Mr. Fila's question to put it in context for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, your observations are noted, Mr. Fila. Thank you. Please continue, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I think -- let me check the transcript because -- yes, you said at line 5 of page 19 today: "In some places perhaps there were indeed those joint actions involving armed population and unarmed Albanian population ..." Who are you referring to when you talk about the unarmed Albanian population, that's just the civilians, correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember mentioning unarmed population. It could be an interpretation error or translation error. I mentioned it the way it's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And here we're talking about --

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Armed non-Siptar population.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And that would have been primarily Serbs, correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, primarily, but not only.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. Fair. And under item number 2, the tasks of the Pristina Corps, the third paragraph in my English version, the second sentence in that paragraph says: "Engage the armed non-Siptar population to secure military facilities and communication lines and protect and defend the non-Siptar population." Correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but not in that order. There must be something wrong with the translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, do you want to read the original and we can have it translated here?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. "Armed non-Siptar population to be engaged to secure military installations and communications, roads, and to protect and defend non-Siptar population."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. That sounds pretty much like the same thing. Maybe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, perhaps the witness -- Mr. Curcin, could you explain how you see that as being any different from what was put to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was a different word order. That sentence began with: "Engage ..." It seems to me that what I had heard earlier is slightly different to what I have read now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is the sense of this not that it's an instruction to the recipient of the document to take authority over or to act with authority over the armed non-Siptar population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I must say this question is complicated for me. Could you make it clearer, perhaps, or maybe divide it into two questions. I didn't understand ultimately who has power over whom. It seems to transpire that the Pristina Corps or the army would have powers over the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Perhaps you could read to us the whole of that third section of section 2. It starts with the words: "With part of the forces ..." The sentence before the one you read, read that along with the sentence which you read.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Right. "With part of the forces prevent the spilling over and withdrawal of Siptar terrorist forces from the Rugovo area to the Metohija area. Engage the armed non-Siptar population to secure military facilities and communication lines and to protect and defend the non-Siptar population."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Curcin, that has been translated into English as an instruction to use part of the forces to prevent spilling over and withdrawal of terrorists and to engage the armed non-Siptar population to secure military facilities and communication line. So it sounds in English like an instruction to the recipient of the document to use the Yugoslav Army for part of the job and the armed non-Siptar population for another part of the job.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, that sounds like telling the recipient that he's in charge of a combined operation involving both the Yugoslav Army and the armed non-Siptar population, which is something you've so far denied is the import of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] With all due respect, I've said I hadn't seen this document before. Last time I was examined on a section of the map and that's the way I answered. As far as armed non-Siptar population is concerned, I firmly believe that it was in fact a part of the Ministry of Defence in the form of civilian defence and civilian protection, personnel whose primary task is to defend themselves. Secondly, to protect and defend more important facilities and installations on that territory and features and roads, communication lines. That was their purpose.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Curcin, I believe we will hear evidence soon that there may have been three lines of command here: The army, the MUP, and the civil protection or civil defence, the way you've described it, commanded through the Ministry of Defence. That's not what we're looking at at the moment. What we're looking at is what this document seems to say, and on the face of it, it seems to be telling the person to whom the order is directed that he has to engage both Yugoslav Army forces and armed non-Siptar population for different parts of a combined operation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Is that a question or an assertion? If it's a question, my answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And I think I would understand you also to be saying that that's not the general position, that the command structure is normally different from that. But what we have to do is work out what this order amounted to. Now, Mr. Hannis will, no doubt, wish to continue. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, General, in fairness to you because you haven't seen this before, let me take you to two other areas where we have some more information about this. Could you go back down to item number 5: "Tasks of units," and you'll see under 5.1 the task: The 125th Motorised Brigade, 2nd Battalion of the 58th light Infantry Brigade are to set up a blockade. And going on to the next paragraph it says: "Task: Support the MUP forces in breaking up and destroying the Siptar terrorist forces along" a certain axis. So doesn't that indicate this a joint operation with the VJ supporting the MUP in their activities of breaking up and destroying the Siptar terrorist forces in that area?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Finally if you could go to item number 13, the last one before the signature block that says: "Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija." Do you find that?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And item 13 says: "Organize joint action with MUP forces regarding the preparation and conduct of combat operations before and during the conduct of combat operations." And the next sentence says: "The Joint Command for Kosovo and Metohija shall command all forces from the Pristina sector during the conduct of combat operations." To me that sounds like a joint operation, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly, because I haven't had this document and I had no chance to deal with it at length. I can only accept what you say.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, based on what parts we read out, do you have any reason to disagree with that viewpoint that it was a joint operation?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Para 3.1 coordinated action with MUP forces. It's obvious that it's about coordinated action, nobody's subordinated to anyone else. It is only to be accepted that there is a separate chain of command for the army and a separate chain of command for the MUP. Maybe they were together at one point in Pristina, but to me it is obvious that it means they were carrying out a joint operation, adhering to their own respective chains of command and their own forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, the map that General Ojdanic had gotten from General Pavkovic, do you know or did General Ojdanic tell you whether that was the only map he brought with him and he left it behind with General Ojdanic or did he have a separate copy of the same map that he took away with him? How did that work?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no, and I've already said that it was just a section of the map, which means that the map was cut up into sections. It was not a complete map with the border. The scale was 1:50.000, as far as I remember, which means that it was depicting a relatively small area on the ground.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But do you know, is that the only copy there was or had General Pavkovic taken away with him a duplicate copy of the same excerpt of a map with the positions of the forces located on it?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know about that. I know that there was only this one map with General Ojdanic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Because if he didn't take away the map, how is he going to know what to do about the suggestions that General Ojdanic made in terms of where forces should be positioned?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would have known that very well because he kept the original at the command. He most probably made a sketch as an auxiliary document that he had taken with him to help him explain, but the original stayed at the command.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And in the suggestions P1487, number 2 says: "Our forces' main objective should be destruction, which you will have difficulty achieving with your current formations under blockade." I thought you told us when you were here last time that the map only showed positions of VJ units and enemy forces. There weren't any MUP units on the map, there weren't any armed non-Siptar population units or elements on the map, correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, nobody asked me about that at the time. I'm certain nobody asked me about either of these things. Armed non-Siptar population could not have been shown on the map and wasn't shown. As far as I remember, there were two or three little patrols of the MUP shown on the map, two or three patrols of unidentified strength drawn in somewhere in the gaps between military units, but certainly not the civilian population.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And the suggestions don't make any mention of what should be done with or how actions should be coordinated with those MUP patrols, does it?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: All right. Based on what we've seen in terms of the number and kinds of documents generated by General Ojdanic as chief of the Supreme Command Staff and the testimony we've heard from several members of the General Staff, of the Supreme Command Staff about the kind of general he was, my impression is that he was a very meticulous, organized, detail-oriented kind of boss. Would you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Completely. This time I agree completely, unlike the previous time.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And it just strikes me as extremely odd that General Ojdanic, chief of the Supreme Command Staff, the highest uniformed soldier in the country, when General Pavkovic comes in after having been with President Milosevic, the supreme commander, brings in an excerpt of a map and basically General Ojdanic drops everything else he's doing on the 17th of April in the middle of the war, calls you in, and makes some suggestions for this map so urgent that there's not time to retype the telegram, he makes a handwritten change, and sends it out. It seems to me he's deferring to a subordinate, he's deferring to this Joint Command, which we don't know where that fits into the general scheme of the chain of command for the army. Why is that? Doesn't that strike you as unusual?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. But there are so many assertions in that question it's difficult for me to respond to all of them properly at once. First of all, that subordinate is the commander of the 3rd Army and he is entitled to carry out operations in his area pursuant to his own decisions, even General Ojdanic, as you said, a principled man in uniform, this is the first time I must confess I had press for General Ojdanic from the Prosecution. Anyway, he didn't want to stop the operation, he didn't want to terminate it, he didn't want to issue an order, he gave suggestions. Why was this urgent? I am beginning to understand this only now. When I saw that the readiness was for the next morning, on the 18th, and only now do I understand why the suggestion said it should be postponed by 24 hours, to the 19th. I tried to understand -- to explain last time but you stopped me. The ground is very hostile in that part of the territory, it's the most difficult terrain in Kosovo and Metohija. It takes several hours to move a unit by several kilometres, especially by night. This was night-time. Units were already in position, and that's why it was urgent, he didn't even want to properly change that one word because that document needed to reach the command of the 3rd Army, from there the command of the Pristina Corps, and go up to stop the operation. As far as I recall, that operation was not carried out at all at that time, it was only carried out sometime around the 20th of May, at least I know that one such operation was carried out around the 20th of May. That may be it. So there's nothing unusual about this. This is quite usual and normal in a war, and General Ojdanic certainly must have been glad to see his commander and exchange a few words with him at the command post. He dropped whatever he was doing and talked to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... There's nothing unusual about this, this is quite usual, how often did something like that happen where General Pavkovic went to see the supreme commander and then came to General Ojdanic and gave him a map and got suggestions from him? This is the only time that happened, is it, or did that happen on a regular basis?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that. No, I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just know about this one particular case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And it was, it was a matter of concern to General Ojdanic what happened with those suggestions, wasn't it, because let's look at Exhibit 3D589 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Before you move, if you don't mind, Mr. Hannis --

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Not at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I would like to be clear to your answer to that last question. You say that -- in response to the suggestion that the subordinate was in charge, you said: "That subordinate is the commander of the 3rd Army and he is entitled to carry out operations in his area pursuant to his own decisions." Now, do you mean to say that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I'm referring to the commander of the 3rd Army, who has the right in his area of responsibility to carry out combat actions on the basis of his decisions, also the commander of the Pristina Corps in his area of responsibility on the basis of the decisions of the commander of the 3rd Army on the basis of yet his own decisions; and he is held responsible for that. May I just say one more sentence? It won't do us any harm. Not all actions are carried out on the basis of decisions and orders of the Supreme Command Staff; they issue a directive and then the subordinate commanders take action.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: In particular you're saying, if we interpret the order as being authority for commanding the armed non-Siptar population, that General Pavkovic was entitled to decide on his own to engage the armed non-Siptar population; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In the suggestions there is no mention of the unarmed non-Siptar population as far as I can remember. I'm making these comments outside that context. I'm only talking about the document that I had occasion to see and testify about. This document is one I saw a few moments ago only, and I cannot give you a proper answer in relation to that; that is why I cannot answer your specific question either.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I don't understand that. You know how the army operates, so just forget for the moment that all you've seen is the suggestions document and tell me as a matter of principle whether you meant to say in your answer that the commander of the 3rd Army can carry out operations in his area pursuant to his own decisions, that would include commanding the armed non-Siptar population?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In certain situations for certain tasks, in a certain area in terms of carrying out a concrete operation he could have given them assignments or tasks, or rather, authorise a subordinate to do that. These are specific orders, that is to say securing facilities of particular importance, securing roads, communication lines, even military facilities as well, protecting the population and material goods. As for these specific tasks, that is what they were used for.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And could that be even without mention of such authority in a directive?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. A commander in his zone of responsibility can bring together all the forces that he has available for carrying out a particular task.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And is that answer confined to combat operations?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, at the time combat operations are being carried out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And, General, regarding the apparent urgency of that telegram regarding the suggestions, I would like to hand you a hard copy of Exhibit 3D589. These are the briefing notes for the evening briefing on the 18th of April, 1999, the next day. And if you could go to I think the next-to-the-last page at the very bottom and then it carries on to the top of the last page. I've highlighted in green item number 6 in English is translated as: "Lieutenant-General Curcin, find out when the telegram was sent to the 3rd Army command," and then on the next page for you it says: "Ask when the telegram was delivered." This is in reference to that telegram regarding suggestions in connection with that Joint Command order, correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, my last question in connection with that topic has to do with the Joint Command. What -- didn't you have some question about what this Joint Command was that was apparently issuing orders for -- from what you could get from the map, either the 3rd Army or the Pristina Corps? You said you never heard of it before, is that right, or you heard mention of it in some collegium meetings but you didn't think much about it?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I said that clearly last time. I heard that at one of the collegium meetings, I think it was the end of January, I heard this mentioned, that question of some kind of Joint Command. I never said, nor will I ever admit, that some kind of Joint Command commanded the 3rd Army. If that was said somewhere and that it was I who allegedly said that, that is not the case.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay, but my question is: As a soldier and the term command has special meaning. Seeing Joint Command order, apparently for either the 3rd Army or the Pristina Corps, didn't that raise some questions in your mind as to what is this Joint Command? Who is it? And what gives it or them the authority to be issuing any kind of orders to some unit within our VJ? That must have raised a question in your mind as a professional soldier.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: I see Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Again, I would kindly ask that if something is put to the witness, it be stated correctly. What is this order of some Joint Command to the 3rd Army, one that I have not seen so far and Mr. Hannis did see it. So could I please have a reference. What is this order of the Joint Command to the 3rd Army that this witness should now explain? You know, Your Honour, that is why it is the right thing to do to give a reference.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]...

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, he only saw a map that referred to the Joint Command. The map was delivered by General Pavkovic, the commander of the 3rd Army, so I think it's not a -- an illogical conclusion to assume that the order must have been for either the 3rd Army or some subordinate element thereof, the Pristina Corps, since it's an operation in the Rugovo area in Kosovo in 1999.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can only conclude that a hen is a rooster, as you put it once. Look at the question, just look at the question. When did you see the Joint Command issue orders to the 3rd Army? Not saying when Thomas Hannis or the Office of the Prosecutor concluded that such and such a thing happened. I am not sure that this Anglo-Saxon system of yours is the best one because in our system we say the truth; if something is white, then it is white. And if you say something different, then that means you're not saying the truth or misleading the witness. Just show one document where a Joint Command is issuing orders to the 3rd Army or withdraw your question. That's the end of the story. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: You can deal with this by referring to the map, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, let me ask it this way then.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, didn't you have a question about who this Joint Command was and for what units it was issuing orders in the VJ? What VJ units it was proposing to command or direct or deploy?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, you're not right at all, unfortunately, for several months now, years, if you wish. No Joint Command commanded army units. This was a body that was used for coordinating joint activities that were being carried out in the same area at the same time by army units and MUP units, and that's the only thing it is. So there is no commanding -- well, there is -- but there is no commanding of the military chain of command over MUP units and the other way around. Army units are not commanded by the MUP. Somebody did this, somebody called this colloquially a Joint Command for some reason, and I know this full well and you mentioned it, so I have a reference now to respond to this as an experienced soldier. It does not have the single attribute that a command has. First of all, it does not have a commander, it does not have organizational establishment structure, it doesn't have a stamp, it doesn't have a seal, it doesn't have an office, it doesn't have its registry, it registers documents under 455 in the command of the Pristina Corps, it doesn't have its security, it doesn't have anything of its own, it just has this joint name, that someone due to some circumstances called the Joint Command. Please, let us deal with this delusion that has been harboured by the Prosecution for so long. Let us dispel it because there is no Joint Command. There is a body for coordinating joint activities --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: This is way too fast for interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: This is not a prosecutorial delusion we have evidence in this case of Joint Command orders issues saying the Joint Command will command operations. Now, I thought you told us before you didn't know about the Joint Command; now you tell us you know that the Joint Command was a coordinating body. How do you know that?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I did prepare for giving evidence here. I thought about it, didn't I, I read something in the newspapers, what the Office of the Prosecutor was asking individual witnesses, things like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, I wondered for a moment, Mr. Curcin, if I had fallen asleep somewhere during your evidence and missed the earlier part where you had told us this, but my recollection is exactly that of Mr. Hannis's, that you gave no indication before of having any knowledge of what the Joint Command actually was. Now you've indicated you know it was some sort of coordinating body. Tell us more about it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very gladly. This is the first time that I have been put such a direct question about this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, let's start with the membership. Who were the members of the Joint Command?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: All right. What did it do then, this non-delusional body?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've already said a few minutes ago to Mr. Hannis that I believe that it actually coordinated action that was being carried out in a particular area at the same time, the army and the police, so that there would not be an exchange of friendly fire. I believe that that was the main job or task and duty.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, can I go back to the question that I started with: Who were the members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Whoever, I don't know who the members were; however, from the indictment I saw who was being charged with that inter alia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you're not here to deal with your assessment or tell us about your assessment of the indictment and what you've been reading and what you've been viewing on television or anywhere else. You're here to answer questions that you're asked from your own personal knowledge. You're not even being asked to tell us things based on the preparation or the proofing that you underwent before you came here to give evidence. Your job is simply to tell us what you know, and you have now created the impression that you know what the Joint Command was. So we would like to know what it is that this Joint Command was, according to you from your personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am sorry that that is the impression you got. I really do not have any in-depth knowledge about this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: You've raised some points about the Joint Command that there wasn't on those Joint Command orders a signature and that the numbering system seems to come from the Pristina Corps. Let me ask you something about that. If you're writing orders to VJ units for combat operations and you have a Joint Command - or if you want to refer to it as a joint coordinating body - you have members on that body that include not only army personnel, commanders; police commander; and civilians. Who best knows among those three groups, the police, the army, and the civilians, who knows best how to write up orders to army units on how to carry out combat operations? It's the army, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is speculation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Mr. Curcin, would you leave the courtroom very briefly while we hear this objection and deal with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, so far the witness when speaking about this command, he knows it, he doesn't know, he talked about the MUP units and the army units. He did not say a single word so far about civilians. And now what is being put to him that this Joint Command has to have the army and the MUP and civilians at that, because that is what the Prosecutor thinks it should be and who is now the most important of the three. When did the man say a single word about civilians? You asked him, Hannis asked him, and he talked about some kind of coordinating body, coordination, to avoid friendly fire between the army and the MUP, and I don't see that the army and the MUP would be firing at this third most important party, the civilians, that was not mentioned so far. Well you cannot really manipulate things that way, you cannot speculate that way as suits you best, that goes a bit beyond allowed limits because civilians were never mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, the witness mentioned hearing about the Joint Command in some of the collegium sessions. I don't have the specific references in front of me, but I recall that in those collegium sessions where there was a mention of that Joint Command or that Joint Command down there, I think in one of those referring to the Podujevo incident in late December of 1998 or early 1999 there was reference to Mr. Sainovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, well you would need to, I think, establish from the witness knowledge of the involvement of civilians before you could put the question the way you've actually put it. So you can ask him. I got nowhere when I asked the composition, but if you ask a specific pointed question about the -- whether civilians were there and have something to back it up, if he is unaware of the position then you could then proceed to the next part of the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I guess let me ask you this, Your Honour, my question I thought was aimed at determining whether or not civilians would be better at writing military combat operation orders for the VJ than VJ or MUP personnel would be, and I think that's a question he can answer without knowing whether civilians were a member of the Joint Command or not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, but you're -- the way you put it, it presupposed there were members on the body who were civilians. Now, I understand that that's not perhaps essential to your question. Mr. Fila, what's being suggested is that the witness can be asked -- can be asked whether a civilian or a soldier would be better at prescribing instructions for the Pristina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is the kind of question that: Who flies better, a pilot or me? Well, once -- the witness said that he may have heard once at a collegium in January about a Joint Command. He never said that he heard of Sainovic or of Podujevo, no, no, no, let the Prosecutor show us the record and let me see that. In the month of January the Prosecutor says that he heard -- well, in January 1999. Now, let Mr. Hannis get --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Fila, that's not the question I'm asking you. You may have answered it in the very first point you made just now. Are you saying it's so obvious that a soldier would be better at writing orders for the army than a civilian that that's a stupid question? Is that your point? Because if everyone agrees that we can move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. FILA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely, that is what I wanted to say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Does anyone dissent from that view? Very well. We can move past that question, Mr. Hannis, if you have something specific in addition the combined exercise you can deal with that after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, I think that's fair. This is something I can argue in submissions. Is this a good time for the break?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It is, but where are we in your cross at the private session stage yet or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have two more topics, one regarding subordination of the MUP and one related to dealings with telephone communications within the Supreme Command.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah. Well, the usher can take the witness now and we'll see him again at 4.15. Mr. Visnjic, do you know the position in relation to the document? Can we deal with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I already sent e-mail to the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Has the matter --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: To Mr. Riaz.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Has the matter been resolved, Mr. Hannis?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Well, I have the position, but I think I need to advise you of what it is because I'm not sure I understand what it means --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Very well, for that we need to be in private session I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The e-mail I received says: "Restriction imposed by government is in it that document should not be used in whole before ICTY, only the part related to the concrete events and acts can be used." Now, the diary goes I think from the 23rd of March, 1999, through, I don't know, it's -- it's some date late in June, I don't recall the ending date. It's beyond the actual signing of the military and technical agreement, so it's D plus 90 I think instead of D plus 78 or 79. I haven't seen the English, but as far as I know I'm only interested in the dates during the war, but I can't tell from this if that means part related to concrete events and acts.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, you're dealing with events recorded in this document, are you?

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yes, I haven't seen the English, Your Honour, but this is a contemporaneous document that was done in the Supreme Command and I want to ask him some foundational questions about how it was kept who kept it in case I want to induce it later when I don't have a foundational witness available.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Visnjic.

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I have nothing to add.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: These --

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I submitted the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yeah, and there can be no problem with the questions that Mr. Hannis intends to ask in relation to the document. In case there should be trouble ahead, you may wish to have the matter clarified. But on the face of it, it's not even a Rule 70 condition that's been -- that has been imposed. I mistakenly, I think, said 4.15. The break will be a bit shorter. We'll come back at ten past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Visnjic, bearing this mind the questions that Mr. Hannis intends to ask about the document, is there any reason why that should be in private session?

utterances.speaker: MR. VISNJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: So please continue, Mr. Hannis.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, I want to move to another topic now.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And if we could show the witness Exhibit 3D670.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: General, this is President Milosevic's -- this relates to President Milosevic's order about subordinating the MUP to the VJ for combat operations. And you remember seeing that and talking about that before, yes?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, you told us that that never actually was carried out and that the VJ Supreme Command Staff did not have effective control of the MUP, that it did not forward orders to the MUP, and didn't receive reports, and there was no exchange of representatives, that's from paragraph 36 of your statement, correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Are you aware that there were efforts made at the lower levels, at the 3rd Army command level and the Pristina Corps level, to effectuate that order for subordination of the MUP? Did you see reports back or information back from the Pristina Corps or the 3rd Army about their efforts in that regard?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, apart from the one that we discussed of the 25th of May during the first session.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Correct. I want to ask you about a couple of others and see if you ever either seen them or seen a summary of their contents in any of the daily reports, operations reports, or combat reports, or otherwise. The first one is Exhibit P1267. I can hand you a hard copy, General. The B/C/S is just one page. And this is an order apparently signed by General Lazarevic dated the 20th April 1999, and it appears to be to his subordinate unit commanders. You'll see it says: "I order," and number one: "Units and organs of the MUP of Serbia in the brigades' zones of responsibility shall be resubordinated to the brigade commands for carrying out combat operations." Do you see that? And he makes reference --

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: He makes reference to the Supreme Command Staff order of the 18th of April, right?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in the preamble of this order and the order of the army command, or rather, the notice, announcement, of the 3rd Army command of the 20th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Now, at the bottom of the page is some delivery information about who all this order went to in a list several subordinate units of the Pristina Corps, some by courier and some in code. And at the very bottom you'll see listed the Pristina MUP staff, correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, and right at the beginning is said purportedly signed. I have to say that this was signed by General Vladimir Lazarevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: But there is some other information at the bottom and it's not clear to me. There's some handwritten information. There's a number 1615 which appears to be an hour or a time in connection with some of those listed units. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that and I know what this means, if that's what you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Yeah, what does that mean?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: This means that at 1615 hours the telegram was sent to this unit, so this is where you put the time when the telegram was sent to a certain unit after its encryption, in order to be able to keep track of it and to know when it arrived or perhaps even better that this arrived at 1615 if it is indeed the case that it was sent to everybody at 15 --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters didn't hear the time that was referenced.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: The interpreters said they didn't hear the time that was referenced at the end of your answer, I guess.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me repeat everything. In the first square stamp it is indicated when the telegram was processed, that was 1440, and that it was sent at 1510. And then below that where you have the addressees it is indicated 1615, 354th Brigade, and 175 Engineers Battalion. I'm not quite sure whether it was sent to them at that time or that they received it at that time, but this was either the time when the telegram was sent or when it was received.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Regarding the Pristina MUP staff it appears that's underlined but I also see a note that says: "Remark the tele or fax has not been sent," and then there's something illegible, perhaps a signature. Do you see that, and can you help us with what that might refer to?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can only assume and I have been asked to tell you only things that I know for sure, but if you want me to speculate I'll do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: No, that's all right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Could we go to Exhibit 1269, P1269.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And I have a hard copy of this one I think that I can hand you. This is a document dated the 8th of May, 1999, from the 3rd Army command signed by General Pavkovic regarding deployment of VJ and MUP forces in combat control of the territory, an order. And handwritten on the first page near the top it says: "Pristina MUP to General Lukic personally." Is that what it says in the handwriting?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I says it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: Okay. And under the order number 1 is: "Engage all forces in the Pristina Corps's zone of responsibility to ensure full control of the territory and permanently passable roads." And then, I want to ask you about item number 7. Can you finding that, General?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And it says, does it not: "In accordance with the situation the disposition of MUP and military district forces," or --

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Military territorial detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: "In the brigades' zones of responsibility may be changed in relation to their current disposition, which I hereby designate as the responsibility of brigade commanders." So it seems that General Pavkovic assumes that he has the authority regarding the disposition of MUP forces and he's delegating that authority to his brigade commanders; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't able to read the whole telegram, so I can only tell you about paragraph 7. So I don't have the full context, but that's what it says here, just the way you read it out.

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
utterances.text: And number 9, would you read it out to be sure we have the translation correct.

utterances.speaker: DJORDJE CURCIN [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 9 reads: "The command of the Pristina Corps and the staff of the Ministry of the Interior shall issue their orders to regulate other issues related to the engagement of the Army of Yugoslavia, the military territorial units, and the units of the Ministry of the Interior and to ensure consistent implementation of this order."

utterances.speaker: MR. HANNIS
