However, as I read this paper that you quoted from here, I'm trying to answer that question of yours, who was the protagonist of the activity involved here, and in this case it was the MUP.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We'll get to that question, General, but I would please direct you to answer the questions I ask and you did that I think with this one. Now, we'll go a lot quicker if we stick with the questions themselves because I will examine everything with you, be rest assured of that. Now, with respect to section -- subsection 2.3, which I believe is on the next page in the B/C/S version. It lists a unit there, the 1st mt and looks like a v, HK. Can we conclude that this is a VJ unit that is referenced in 2.3, first of all?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Can we also conclude in 2.3 that there's not any MUP unit or organ referenced with respect to this particular task?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: In that paragraph, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then am I correct in concluding that with respect to this particular task, in this particular VJ unit is to carry out an independent attack in a particular area without any police involvement?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, at this locality, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Who would be the protagonist of the activity involved then?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: I didn't hear you.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Who would then be the protagonist of this activity or action, the one mentioned in 2.3?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: In 2.3 it would be the combat group that is mentioned above.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [In English] Now, we've had some discussions, some confusion with other witnesses regarding -- as I hope it will be easy to clear up. Am I correct that according to military doctrine of the VJ it would be inconceivable to have a police officer, irrespective of rank or position, commanding over VJ units; that is to say, only an army officer can command over VJ units?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, a military officer never commands the police and a police officer never commands the military. In the system of coordination, it is established who is the main party in charge and who has an auxiliary role. Then every system gets assignments down their own chain or line. However, coordination spells this out precisely.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, we need to clear up some more military terminology. If you look at section 2.4, which should be on the next page in the English but on the same page in the B/C/S. If you can help us with simplifying or explaining in detail the meaning of the task for BG-125-3, which in B/C/S says: [Interpretation] "In coordinated action in the 10th MUP Detachment, attacks against the Prilep village - Rznic village and Prilep village - Glodjane village."

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, the third group got the task to attack along that axes and the 30th MUP detachment will act in concert with them, so it is the combat group of the 125th Brigade that is in charge of that action and the MUP acts in a coordinated fashion with them.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: I think you touched on this earlier in talking about what an "odluka" or decision is and you mentioned the "zapovest" or order of a commander. Now, with respect to combat actions, am I correct that the "zapovest" is a command document delivered in written form covering larger formations of units for terms of combat activities?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: No. "Zapovest," an order, is issued even at the lowest levels, but orally, verbally. For example, a squad order, a company leader, et cetera, issue oral orders, whereas higher command issue orders in writing.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's what I was focusing on. "Zapovesti" for higher command issues, for instance, where multiple units are involved. Now, the issuance --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we're perhaps at cross-purposes. The witness is quite clear that "zapovest" is an oral order. Are you content with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour, actually he said that it was always in writing when it's a higher command, that was the last part of his answer. Perhaps I can ask him to clear it up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Just let me read this.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: That's why I tried to use the Serbian terminology because in the translations things can get confusing because there's multiple terminology for essentially similar actions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. So it's oral at the lowest level and written at the higher level. Now I follow. Thank you. You don't need to clarify that.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Now, with respect to the higher level commands that -- higher-level orders, excuse me, higher-level "zapovesti" am I correct that the commander drafting the "zapovest" is effectuating his command over the units specified in the "zapovest" as having tasks?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: Well, not necessarily. Namely, that his command powers pertain only to -- to all units, rather, only he directly issues tasks to his subordinate units, his subordinates. He can also mention those with whom he acts in concert, in coordinated action, those who are not directly subordinated to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues]... Enemy forces to say where they're located. Let's return to the "odluka" for a second. With respect to the "odluka," the example we saw was in written form. Am I correct that it was the -- within the practice of the VJ for such "odlukas" to also be reproduced on to maps; and if so, would the information from the map "odluka" provide the forces with information on how to carry out their tasks in anti-terrorist actions?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: That cannot be seen on a map. Details cannot be seen on a map, only the idea, the basic idea, can be seen on a map. Any graphic representation on a map is simplification, and only the basic elements of the concept can be seen there and the basic idea. Details cannot be seen; that is why orders are written, otherwise they would not be written out, otherwise they would be done as maps and then the maps would be handed out, whereas written orders give far more detail than a map does.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And with respect to the "odlukas," perhaps we should pull up an example so we can have it in front of us as we're talking about it. 5D1175 I believe is one that has already been introduced into evidence by one of my colleagues. Once this comes up, sir, we'll take a look at it, but I believe this to be an "odluka" map dealing with the action Voksa from 1998.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: I can't see anything yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: We'll have to wait a moment. There we go. Now, sir, based on your knowledge and experience, can you derive from this "odluka" the basic instructions, the "osovni deja" [phoen] being conveyed by this "odluka" for the stated action? I mean, is it possible to determine the basic location and planned activities of the units?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: On the basis of this document, one can see the position of the units and what units were engaged. And one can see from the symbols representing these units what the basic purpose is, basic intention, attack or defence. That can be distinguished, nothing else. Yes, you can also see here who gives the approval for this decision. There is also a legend, a key, as to what the forces involved are. And then also the commander's signature in the lower right-hand corner. However, only the contours of the deployment of the units can be seen, nothing more than that. That is why the decision always accompanies the order concerned. It spells out the engagement of the unit in carrying out a particular task.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Just to clear up one thing related to your last answer. Am I correct that the commander who signs on the lower right-hand corner is the commander charged with creating this map "odluka," for planning the action?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: Not necessarily. It is signed by the person who did this, who drew this graphically, or rather, in whose name it was done. It doesn't have to be the commander in person, it's his team, his staff, but he signs it as his own document. However, it does not necessarily mean that he is the commander in charge of that action.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And then the --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: Because -- because, if you allow me, if he were the protagonist of this activity, then he would sign it "commander of such and such for such and such an action." As it says here decision for crushing Siptar terrorist forces in the Voksa region, it is only from the legend that we can see who would be involved.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: And the upper left-hand corner is the commander who approved this proposed action; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, Mr. Cepic, are you going to let us in on the secret?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: First to clarify with my learned friend, Mr. Ivetic. With your leave, Your Honour, page 97, line 21, who would be involved, I think that witness said: [Interpretation] Who would be the protagonist of the activity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: It's 7.00, Your Honour. I'm not done; I think that's obvious.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: This isn't for the purpose of being restrictive, but for guidance on how we plan the rest of the week. Can you give any indication of how long you might take?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, my previous estimate was in the range of two hours, so I think I've spent approximately half an hour thus far, so we should be an hour and a half remaining tomorrow for my part of it, again if things go as smoothly as they have thus far.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Mr. Stamp, do you envisage your cross-examination being more than a day?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: Possibly just a little bit more, but I'll try to keep it to a day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Okay. Not with a view to -- again, to being restrictive, but just trying to make sensible use of the week. Mr. Ackerman, is the position about the non-availability of any witnesses this week for your case entirely clear or still in some doubt?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I think it's very clear, Your Honour, that we can't get anybody here -- we can't actually put a witness on until Monday. We may be able to get somebody here, but we've got problems beyond just getting them here. We're working on them. Mr. Fila has been of assistance to try to get some of those solved. We've planning on the 22nd for a long time, and just when everything breaks so that there's nobody here to talk to, it becomes clear that we might try to get somebody here Friday, and we did try, we went into some great efforts, but I don't think we can get it done -- in fact, I know we can't.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Would it assist you, Mr. Stamp, if you had a clear indication that you wouldn't be required to cross-examine until Thursday?

utterances.speaker: MR. STAMP
utterances.text: We would be very grateful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: It may be that that's how it's going to work out anyway, it's not clear, but we may be able to give you that indication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, we can assure Mr. Stamp that he will not be required to cross-examine tomorrow, but it would be very helpful if the Prosecution were in a position to cross-examine on Thursday, bearing in mind there's a possibility of spilling over into Friday, and I suspect that that is inevitable in this situation. Mr. Radinovic, we have to stop for the evening at this point. We will resume tomorrow, and that will be at 9.00 tomorrow morning. It's not clear whether you will be here for the full session or whether we will have to simply stop early and re-commence on Thursday. But I can tell you now that you will be here until at least Thursday and possibly Friday. Overnight it is important that you have no discussion with anyone at all about the evidence in this case. You can talk about whatever you like with whomsoever you choose to speak to, but you must talk about any subject other than the evidence; the evidence is off limits. Could you now please leave the courtroom with the usher, and we shall see you tomorrow morning at 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
